name: compiled effects, colour grading and the post-process chain, in a browser
environment: CNA_WASM_ARTIFACT_DIR must point at a CNA wasm artifact built with -DCNA_EASYGL_COMPILED_EFFECTS=ON -DCNA_CNAEXT=ON, and CNA_SOURCE_PATH at a cnanext checkout for the .fxb fixture. All but the last mutant are in the WebAssembly backend, because the shared managed half is already covered by compiled-effect-render.json against the windowed build and what is unproved here is the wasm32 half: the tagged-value writes, the pointer-and-handle struct layouts, and the routes this slice newly resolves. The last one is deliberately in the shared managed Effect, to show that this browser scenario really does run through it rather than through some browser-only path -- eight wasm mutants dying would otherwise be consistent with a page that had reimplemented the API it was supposed to be testing.

mutants.why: a scalar or vector parameter is accepted and never written into CNA's storage, so the shader keeps the value the .fxb declared -- the defect that looks exactly like a working SetValue
mutants.replace: void parameter; void valueType; void pointer;

mutants.why: a Vector4 writes three components, so Tint's alpha is whatever the previous allocation held; the RGB channels stay correct, which is what makes a three-channel assertion pass this
SetValue(number[]) sends element zero and leaves the rest at their declared values, so Weights[1] never moves -- and both draws that differ only in Weights become identical
Apply() binds nothing, so whichever program the device last had stays bound
CurrentTechnique is stored managed and never selected natively, so both techniques draw whichever one CNA had current
a struct parameter reflects no members, so Lighting.Intensity cannot be reached at all -- the shape a reflection that stopped one level short would have

the exact mistake docs/c-api/WASM_ARTIFACT.md warns a binding will make: CNA_UserPrimitives written at the native offsets, where vertex_data is eight bytes wide and the declaration handle lands where wasm32 puts the padding
half the quad is drawn, which leaves the sampled centre texel on the diagonal between the two triangles -- a geometry defect a pass/fail on 'did it throw' cannot see
the same anchor compiled-effect-render.json mutates for the windowed build: if this kills the browser suite too, both backends reach one managed Effect rather than two that resemble each other
mutants.replace: void backend; void handle; void described;

mutants.why: the context is populated without CNA's own initializer, so struct_size and struct_version are zero and its four camera matrices are singular rather than the identity -- the shape a binding that treated a growable descriptor as a plain struct would have
Strength is stored managed and never sent, so the half-strength and zero-strength draws both come back fully graded -- a defect the full-strength assertion alone cannot see
the table is never bound, so every grade returns the source and the pass looks like a working blit

a CNA_Vector3 read back as (Y,X,Z): the cube's entries come out permuted, which the read-back-before-any-pixel assertion catches and no pixel assertion would, because the table CNA holds is still right
mutants.find: return { X: view.getFloat32(out, true), Y: view.getFloat32(out + 4, true), Z: view.getFloat32(out + 8, true) };
mutants.replace: return { X: view.getFloat32(out + 4, true), Y: view.getFloat32(out, true), Z: view.getFloat32(out + 8, true) };

mutants.why: the destination render target is dropped, so the blit draws to the back buffer and the target the test reads stays whatever it was -- a draw that succeeds and lands nowhere the caller asked
mutants.find: "cna_fullscreen_pass_draw", pass, source, destination, effect, width, height, 0,

mutants.why: the chain accepts a pass and holds none, so its pass count stays zero and applying it produces whatever an empty chain does rather than the composed grade
a chain handle sent to cna_post_process_pass_apply: the two routes take the same context and differ only in what the first argument is, which is exactly the confusion a route table makes easy
every pass and the chain draw to the back buffer instead of the target the caller named -- a whole family of draws that succeed and land nowhere, from one field of a shared descriptor
